name: DNA language model inference throughput and maximum batch size on one A100 80 GB by sequence length (Aspidova et al. 2026 Table 2)
description: Maximum batch size that fits in memory and mean throughput over 10 timing runs for nine encoder configurations.

attributes.protocol: For each sequence length L, the maximum batch size that fits in memory is found by exponential growth until an error, then binary search; throughput in tokens/s is averaged over 10 timing runs at that batch size on one NVIDIA A100 (80 GB).
limitations: Author-reported: the authors develop ModernGENA and GENA-LM; DNABERT-2 and NTv2 were run by them.

The printed tokens/s values are inconsistent with the printed batch sizes and the stated pretraining throughput (1.33M tokens/s on eight A100s, Section 3.2.4); the source carries an evidence concern, and values are kept as printed.
Inputs are fixed-length sequences whose content is not described; throughput does not depend on biology, but the input source is not stated.
Throughput is the mean of 10 timing runs; no spread is printed.
Models tokenize differently (BPE, 6-mer), so the same token length covers different numbers of base pairs.
GENA base and large print no values from 1,024 tokens upwards.

evidence_concerns.message: Appendix B Table 2 and Figure 1 (axis 'Inference speed (tokens/s)') give throughput in tokens/s, but the printed values are inconsistent with the printed batch sizes: ModernGENA base (FA2 + autocast bf16) at L = 256 prints 552.44 tokens/s with a batch of 3,631 sequences (929,536 tokens), about 28 minutes per batch, and ModernGENA base without FA2 at L = 8192 prints 71.15 tokens/s with a batch of 92 (753,664 tokens), about 2.9 hours per batch, against a stated pretraining throughput of 1.33M tokens/s on eight A100 GPUs (Section 3.2.4). The unit or scale of the throughput column is unclear. Batch sizes share the table. Values are recorded as printed.
